tdd-under-pressure.verdict: inconclusive (27/100 vs 31/100, p=0.64 — need more runs)

interpretation: The TDD-skill restore did NOT recover the behaviour. Behavioural pass (bug fixed AND a covering test written) under explicit 'don't spend time on tests' pressure: with = 56/100, identical to the 56/100 measured BEFORE the restore. ref:4f6815f measured 76/100 on 2026-08-03 and 68/100 here — 8pp of pure noise on the same commit, which is the instrument's between-run variance at n=100. Pooling the two ref runs (144/200 = 72%) against the post-restore with arm gives Fisher p=0.0065. So the 2026-08-03 compression regression is real and something OTHER than skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md caused it. Re-graded all 200 surviving scratch projects with check 3 corrected (the shipped check only searched the first test file containing '100', so a regression test written in a NEW file scored as absent); the corrected grader returns the identical 68/56, so that defect did not confound this result.
